text:
ryan: Heads-up  perf alert: host-side p99 jumped ~18% for small streaming requests after last KV warmup tweak. Traces point to repeated prefix scans + writev syscalls.

mei: repro steps? pool?

ryan: repro on dedicated-low-latency. Use chunked transfer and many tiny messages. curl example: curl -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate

carlos: flame top: parse::validate_prefix (30%), tokenizer::fast_scan (20%), kv::warm_prefix (18%), grpc::writev (14%), batching::select (10%), other 8%.

mei: sounds like warm_prefix is running per-request before the ingress has a chance to coalesce chunks. Kernel picker then picks fallback kernel because token stream looks fragmented, causing copies.

ryan: idea: delay warm_prefix until after a short coalesce window (1-2ms) or attach a per-connection prefix cache (memoize first 4kb). Short-term we can gate warm_prefix for tiny requests.

carlos: agree. I've opened PR with a conservative gate: if total_len < 2048 && chunk_count < 3 then skip and emit metric parse.warm_skipped. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4720

ops-bot: canary started on pool=dedicated-low-latency-canary, hosts=4, image=runtime:pr-4720, ramp=30m, dashboard=https://canary.redwood.dev/4720

mei: while canary runs I'll prototype an incremental prefix cache plus a kernel-picker hint when fragmentation is detected so we avoid fallback copies.

ryan: added small perf harness test that simulates fragmented frames + kv warmup to prevent regressions.

carlos: early canary (12m): p95 -7%, p99 -11%, host CPU -6%. parse.warm_skipped ~= 58% for tiny requests.

mei: good. Next: 3h data, land incremental connection cache, and consider ingress proxy micro-coalesce to reduce writev frequency.

ryan: snippet from PR: if (total_len < 2048 && chunk_count < 3) { metrics.inc("parse.warm_skipped"); return; }

ops-bot: ticket INF-1312 created to track follow-ups (incremental cache, kernel hint, ingress coalesce).

mei: thanks team. Keep an eye on kernel.choice telemetry after cache lands.
